thread_title: S. leucophylla Hurricane creek white Clone D
breadcrumb: S. leucophylla Hurricane creek white Clone D

posts.body_html:
For those of you who are not familar with Hurricane creek white, here's a link to the story and their status in the wild: sarracenia.proboards.com/thread/921/remains-original-hurricane-creek-white

Surprisingly, S. leucophylla Hurricane creek white clone D hasn't had a thread of its own until until now! In a previous leucophylla thread ( sarracenia.proboards.com/thread/1391/leucophylla-var-alba-baldwin-clone ), it was mentioned that some S. leucophyllas grown outdoors in Northern California this year produced what appears to be fall traps about 1-2 months early! S. leucophylla hurricane creek white clone D was one of them!

These traps are regular sized, but a few years ago, this clone produced MONSTER sized traps! Photos taken 8/1/14:

posts.body_html: A nice balanced variation. I like the green webbing. MW you've been able to highlight in previous posts the variability of the HCW plants from season to season, including some clones that have presented as the 'all white' style one season then presenting a red element the next. Is this the case with this clone? Even if it hasn't shown red before, have you found it changes from year to year so far?
